Bay
bā
n. and adj. (an inlet of the sea — in Hebrew a tongue; a reddish-brown horse; and the bay tree)
Three unrelated words share the spelling. The geographic bay renders Hebrew lashon, a tongue of the sea; the bay horse is a reddish colour; and the bay tree is the laurel, an evergreen.

Biblical Definition

Joshua's land survey uses the word for the tongues of the Dead Sea: Judah's south border ran “from the shore of the salt sea, from the bay that looketh southward” (Jos 15:2), and the northern border “from the bay of the sea at the uttermost part of Jordan” (Jos 15:5); Benjamin's went out “at the north bay of the salt sea” (Jos 18:19). The Hebrew is lashon, a tongue — the sea putting out a tongue of water into the land. The most quoted use is the psalm's: “I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree” (Psa 37:35). The bay is the laurel, evergreen, never bare, with no visible season of decline — the perfect image of a prosperity that appears immune to time. The next verse finishes it: yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found. The whole psalm is written to a believer fretting over the prosperity of the wicked, and its counsel is patience with a horizon. And Zechariah's fourth chariot has “grisled and bay horses” (Zec 6:3), which go forth to walk to and fro through the earth (Zec 6:7) — the four winds of heaven, standing before the Lord of all the earth, patrolling.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines bay as an arm of the sea extending into the land; as an adjective, red or reddish, inclining to a chestnut color, applied to horses; and the bay tree as the laurel.

expand to see more

BAY, n. An arm of the sea, extending into the land, not of any definite form, but smaller than a gulf, and larger than a creek.

BAY, a. Red, or reddish, inclining to a chestnut color; applied to the color of horses.

BAY, n. The laurel tree; whence bays, an honorary garland or crown, bestowed as a prize for victory.

LAUREL, n. A tree of the genus Laurus; an evergreen.

Key Scripture

Psa 37:35 — "I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree."

Jos 15:2 — "And their south border was from the shore of the salt sea, from the bay that looketh southward:"

Zec 6:3 — "And in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot grisled and bay horses."

Jos 18:19 — "And the border passed along to the side of Bethhoglah northward: and the outgoings of the border were at the north bay of the salt sea at the south end of Jordan: this was the south coast."

Modern Corruption

The visible flourishing of the ungodly is taken as the last word; Psalm 37 grants the observation and moves the horizon.

expand to see more

Psalm 37 is written for a believer with a specific complaint: the wicked prosper, and it does not appear to matter what anyone does about it. The psalm never denies the observation — I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree — and the evergreen is exactly the right image, since a laurel has no bare season to give the game away. What the psalm does is extend the timeline: fret not thyself because of evildoers… for they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and then, one verse after the bay tree, he passed away, and, lo, he was not.

The pastoral instruction attached is worth naming, because it is not what most people would guess. The psalm does not tell the fretting believer to campaign, expose or avenge. It tells him to trust in the LORD, and do good; delight thyself also in the LORD; commit thy way unto him; rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him. Envy of the prospering wicked is treated as a spiritual danger to the one who envies — fret not thyself in any wise to do evil — and the cure is occupation with God and with one's own duty.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew lashon (H3956), a tongue — a tongue of the sea, a bay; 'ezrach (H249), a native tree, rendered bay tree; 'amots (H554), strong or bay-coloured.

expand to see more

Hebrew lashon (H3956) — a tongue; Joshua 15:2, 15:5, 18:19 — the sea's tongue reaching into the land.

Hebrew 'ezrach (H249) — a native, one born in the land; Psalm 37:35, a tree native to its soil, rendered green bay tree.

Hebrew 'amots (H554) — strong, and by extension bay-coloured; Zechariah 6:3, 6:7, of the fourth chariot's horses.

Hebrew yam hammelach — the salt sea, the Dead Sea; the water these bays belong to.

Hebrew 'arits (H6184) — terrible, ruthless, a man of violence; Psalm 37:35, the wicked in great power.

Usage

"“Spreading himself like a green bay tree” — an evergreen has no bare season."

"“From the bay that looketh southward” — a tongue of the salt sea."

"“Grisled and bay horses” — the fourth chariot of the vision."
